RAR4 and RAR5 test archives are decoded from the libarchive project's public
test fixtures under libarchive/test:
https://github.com/libarchive/libarchive/blob/master/libarchive/test/test_read_format_rar.rar.uu
https://github.com/libarchive/libarchive/blob/master/libarchive/test/test_read_format_rar5_stored_manyfiles.rar.uu

rar4-sample.rar SHA-256 D421B86F6290AEFAD61B2A36737253B2B30FE27C156BD95ABFC230F24FE0307E
rar5-sample.rar SHA-256 62687F5B5050C71A754F479DDA3803CB06359FDFA7AF4E62287ED4AC4ED38E8D

These fixtures are used only in development tests; they are not included in
the application installer.

The additional rar/ fixtures are decoded from the .uu files of the same name
under libarchive/test at commit 115ce76456c3cb65a5fa2ccc08f81684d4ba5bf5:
https://github.com/libarchive/libarchive/tree/115ce76456c3cb65a5fa2ccc08f81684d4ba5bf5/libarchive/test
rar/manifest.json records the decoded filenames, sizes and SHA-256 hashes.
rar/COPYING retains the upstream license. Encryption expectations are from
test_read_format_rar_encryption.c at that commit: four 18-byte text files;
the non-solid visible-name sample uses password/password2 for b.txt/d.txt;
the other encrypted samples use password for all files.
The two multivolume families have extracted-output SHA-256 expectations in
tests/archive-rar.cjs, independently obtained using local 7-Zip 25.01.
The tests only read these contents and never run extracted executables.
The RAR5 CMT/UTF-8 sample is generated by the test from the public RARLAB
format specification: https://www.rarlab.com/technote.htm
